title: Prove legal GL2 bases do not lower the G20 boundary below 38 ADDs.
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Scoped negative result; no new κ. On the pinned PR5840 controller, a basis change preserves the labeled target diagonal exactly when it is an independent `GL(2, F2)` action on each of the 16 equal-monomial coordinate pairs. Every such action still needs at least 38 scratch-free unit binary ADDs on each 32-wire side. The published words meet 38, so the two-sided invoice stays 76 ADDs per port.

This is a counting bound for that commutant, not a helper split, a changed recursive profile, or a selected-frontier update. Selected conditional κ and its five framework assumptions stay as they are.

## Task and overlap

- Base: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8.
- Task: `bit-helper-contract`, scope changed. The card asks for a changed helper path or target split. The live open question on this boundary is the legal-GL(2) question left by `research/g20-full-boundary-floor` and `research/g20-target-pair-boundaries`.
- Live input: `research/g20-isolated-exchange-floor/inputs/CONTROLLER.json` (SHA256 `978536e852c0cfbc150f143e19d2cfddbb434bac6017d914974eb99f641593a8`).
- Nearest work: JoyboyBrian's fixed-endpoint 38-ADD theorem, Ali Romman's equal-target construction, Charan .'s isolated-exchange floor, and Nick Petalas's 18-wire chain floor. Those results either freeze the endpoint or leave this commutant open. Unpaidmoon's earlier G20 notes (short conjugations, port-0 tariff, frame round trip, PR5708 admission) and ToikY's occupied-bank census are different cuts.
- No open PR found whose title or body takes this commutant question.

## Validation

```sh
python3 -I -W error -B research/g20-gl2-commutant-floor/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/g20-gl2-commutant-floor
```

Both registered commands pass and print `PASS_G20_GL2_COMMUTANT_FLOOR`. The partition dynamic program is the proof that the minimum is 20 on the chain block and 18 on the exchange block. Forty-eight direct samples match the split. While developing the check, all `6^7` exchange matrices and all `6^9` chain matrices were also enumerated; those runs are not part of the registered replay. The literal programs replay to the stored matrices at length 38.

Not run: scratch search, gates outside the 32 wires, native/caller/compiler replay, Lean, and a selected-frontier replay.

## Credit

Ali Romman (PR5840 and the equal-target conjugation), Charan . (PR5851 controller retention), Nick Petalas (chain component), JoyboyBrian (fixed-endpoint question), and Alan Bu, Evan Fan, and Robert Joo (the counting bound). Retained target-pair lineage includes PR5834, PR5807/5828, PR5708/5671, ai-nanachi PR5512, Dugongue, and ToikY.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Can one priced scratch wire, or one gate that leaves these 32 wires, lower either legal commutant side below 38 unit ADDs? Fix the scratch tariff and test the four-wire endpoint corner first. An unpriced scratch wire is not a saving.
